attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post. 'As I've argued previously' repeats his own earlier position; he is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The draft keeps 'vast majority', the recent revenue surge, experimental spending, and Anthropic not giving clear visibility into token spend. It drops the slur 'paypigs', which is rhetoric. The language is firm, so this is an observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: incremental revenue, an overwhelming share, and both conditions applying to the same spending. The March–May 2026 window is the evaluator's choice, but the result does not depend on it, because no breakdown exists for any window. Saying that reporting tools existing is not enough is fair.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own release notes, dated August 2025, show a Usage & Cost API existed. Under the contract, tools merely existing does not decide visibility. The note says nothing about whether they were adequate for the customers behind the surge, or what share of revenue those customers made up.

The S-1 was filed 2026-10-26, before the evaluation date. It covers the first half of 2026 year on year and gives qualitative reasons for growth. It does not separate experimental from established use or link spending to visibility. Its period also differs from the contract's window. It is a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: The claim is firm and can be checked in principle. But the packet has no revenue-weighted breakdown of Anthropic's incremental revenue by experimental versus production use, and none by whether customers could see their spend. e1 shows reporting tools existed, which the contract says does not decide the question. e2 gives qualitative growth reasons for a broader period. Neither supports nor contradicts the 'vast majority' share.
